solarEruptions.source: NASA DONKI / Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office · experimental WSA-ENLIL forecasts

entries.note: Narrow CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-11-28T16:36Z. This CME is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely near the E limb and related to field line movement over the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting as early as 2026-11-28T12:39Z.

The best source candidate for this CME is some field line movement followed by dimming and localized brightening centered around N16E64 beginning around 2026-11-28T06:49Z in SDO AIA 193. Based on triangulated measurements, there is a fair amount of westward deflection. There is a brighter, inner feature that follows the initial leading edge, but there does not appear to be an additional source beyond those listed.

A fast narrow jet seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and early timestamps of GOES CCOR-1 and very faintly in one timestamp of C3.  It is covered by the data gap in STEREO A COR2. Its source is likely a very thin filament eruption seen starting ~2026-11-27T21:56Z in GOES SUVI 304 and SDO AIA 304/171, from near AR 14584 (S19E67).

A very faint CME with the loop-like front partially seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in other coronagraphs. It is overlapping with earlier 2026-11-27T19:36Z CME. No source has been found for this CME in EUV imagery.

Faint loop-like CME (or rather part of the front) seen in the NNE, to the NW of the brighter preceding CME: 2026-11-27T19:00Z, as seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 that is having poor quality imagery at the time. It is followed by an even more northern, fainter front first seen starting at 2026-11-27T20:12Z. A very speculative possible source could be the slow, wide filament best seen in SDO AIA 171 behind the NE limb, very slowly detaching some time after 2026-11-27T18Z. No on-disk alternative source has been found, so the CME is likely far-sided.

Bright, fast, two-lobed CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and later in C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Its source is the large, fast prominence eruption seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304/284 after 2026-11-27T18:45Z in association with the C3.9-class flare from near to AR 14584 peaking at 2026-11-27T18:49Z, centered (~S07E69). It is also seen very faintly to the E in a bad (unusable) STEREO A EUV 304 imagery right after the data gap. The C3.9 flare is preceded by a C1.9 flare from the same Active Region (S12E72) peaking at 2026-11-27T18:19Z, which might be the explanation for the two distinct lobes of the same CME. The Active Region 14584 is located to the north of the large northern CH stretching along latitude S22, which might explain the northern deflection of the prominence and of the CME from the flare location.

A faint, very slow CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 and very faintly in C3 and not seen in STEREO A COR2, partly because STEREO A had a data gap and some poor imagery. The start of the CME may be earlier. The CME may be associated with an eruption seen around S10W110-W120 in STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery at 2026-11-27T13:45Z, also seen as a very faint movement of field lines far behind the W limb seen in GOES SUVI 284 after 14:30Z. The CME seems to accelerate a little with time.

Narrow CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. The potential source is a C1.6 flare peaking at 2026-11-27T14:13Z from AR 14584 (S10E75) best seen in SDO AIA 131 imagery. The associated eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 193/304 imagery. The eruption is not visible from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery.

CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and the north in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is a high latitude eruption seen on the north limb, around W15, seen in GOES SUVI 284/304 and SDO AIA 304 imagery starting around 2026-11-27T13:20Z. Moving/opening field lines are best seen in GOES SUVI 284. It is unclear if this eruption is on the disk as seen in GOES SUVI and SDO AIA imagery or if it is far-sided.

CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-11-27T12:45Z. The potential source is unclear, but may be a region of dimming seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting at 2026-11-27T05:37Z or an eruption around S05E70 starting at 2026-11-27T09:36Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery.

CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is an eruption from the vicinity of AR 14582 (N18E19) best seen from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery on the NE limb starting at 2026-11-27T06:45Z. The eruption can also faintly be seen in SDO AIA 193 as dimming.

CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph imagery. The potential source is an eruption near the east limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery around S10E60 starting at 2026-11-26T21:48Z.

Bright CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-26T21:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The CME is seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 following a data gap from 2026-11-26T20:09Z to 2026-11-27T02:09Z. The source of this event is likely beyond the East limb as seen from SDO/GOES and can be seen as field line rising and opening in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-11-26T21:28Z.

Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-26T17:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is a small eruption originating from Active Region 14582 (N18E26) beginning at approx. 2026-11-26T16:12Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193.

CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is filament ejecta and field line movement from around S05E90 deflecting sharply northeastward, as observed in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 starting around 2026-11-26T14:48Z.

CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely on the E limb around S12E90, observed as weak field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-11-26T09:58Z, and in SDO AIA 131 as a B2.7 flare peaking at 2026-11-26T10:02Z from this unnumbered region.

CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and not in STEREO A COR2 likely due to faintness and/or behind occulting disk. The source may be some weak field line movement on/beyond the E limb in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-11-26T07:40Z following a B2.5 flare peaking at 2026-11-26T07:39Z as observed in SDO AIA 131.

CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is on the E limb around S12E90, observed as field line movement and filament ejecta in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-11-26T04:58Z, and in SDO AIA 131 as a B6.4 flare peaking at 2026-11-26T05:07Z from this unnumbered region.

CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and not in STEREO A COR2 likely due to faintness and/or behind occulting disk. No direct source is observed, with the best candidate as some weak field line movement on/beyond the E limb in GOES SUVI 284 around 2026-11-26T02:44Z. Partially overlaps with earlier CME: 2026-11-26T02:12Z.

CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and faintly in STEREO A COR2 with some poor quality background imagery. The source appears to be just on/near the E limb with field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-11-26T02:09Z, noting this is close to the first observation in LASCO C2 but is the best candidate. Partially overlaps with later CME: 2026-11-26T03:48Z.

Narrow CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-26T00:36Z. This CME fades before leaving the field-of-view of C2 and is therefore not seen in any other coronagraphs. The source of this event is a narrow filament eruption originating from beyond the Eastern limb in GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-11-25T22:12Z.

Narrow, faint CME first seen to the Southeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-25T21:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-25T15:38Z. The source of this event is likely far sided, but minor field line movement can be seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-11-25T21:34Z.

Narrow CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-25T20:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-25T15:38Z. The source of this event is a narrow piece of filament ejecta seen originating from along or just beyond the East limb in GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-11-25T20:20Z.

CME first seen to the North by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-11-19:45Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 following a data gap which ended at 2026-11-25T20:12Z. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-25T15:38Z. The source of this event is an eruption from Active Region 14582 (N19E42) beginning at approx. 2026-11-25T17:24Z in SDO AIA 193. Dimming and field line opening can be seen directed almost directly Northward from the region in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284, suggesting heavy Northern deflection.

Narrow CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-25T18:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-25T15:38Z. The source of this event is a narrow piece of filament ejecta seen originating from along or just beyond the East limb in GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-11-25T18:30Z.

Narrow, faint CME first seen to the Southeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-25T18:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-25T15:38Z. The source of this event is likely far sided, but minor field line movement can be seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-11-25T17:30Z.

CME observed to the SSE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and SSW in STEREO A COR2 with a data gap between 2026-11-25T13:23Z through 2026-11-25T15:38Z. The source is far-sided, likely observed as field line movement in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting as early as 2026-11-25T09:55Z over the far SSW limb.

Faint CME observed to the SE only in STEREO A COR2. The source may be one of two weak, slow dimming regions in SDO AIA 193, one centered ~S40E05 from roughly 2026-11-25T03:00Z to 2026-11-25T10:00Z, and the other AR 14581 starting around 2026-11-25T07:09Z, neither very eruptive to discern between.

CME observed to the SSE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and SSW in STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided, maybe field line movement observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting as early as 2026-11-25T04:25Z over the far SSW limb.

CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is an eruption from AR 14582 starting around 2026-11-25T04:25, observed as dimming/field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193 centered around N21E55.

Faint CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2, perhaps due to being a narrow CME directed towards the SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. The only potential on-disk source is a weak dimming centered around N05E15 starting around 2026-11-25T02:33Z in SDO AIA 193, in proximity to a coronal hole centered around S03W10.
Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No distinct source is observed and is likely far-sided.

CME visible to the SE in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2, and a data gap starts in STEREO A COR2 imagery starting at 2026-11-24T21:23Z. There is no clear source for this CME, and it is likely farsided.

Narrow CME faintly visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is also seen to the SSE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is not clear, but there may be an eruption beyond the E limb faintly seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting at 2026-11-24T15:20Z.

CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-11-22T07:48Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There are two notable features to this CME - a narrower, brighter, bulk-like feature and a wider, fainter, shock-like feature. There is not a good source candidate for this CME on the Earth-facing disk, so the source may be far-sided with a significant amount of deflection.

CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-11-22T03:48Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and in a single, late frame in STEREO A COR2. The majority of the CME is missed in STEREO A COR2 due to a real-time data gap from 2026-11-21T05:53Z to 2026-11-22T06:09Z. There are two notable features of this CME - a bright, narrow, bulk-like feature and a faint, wide, shock-like feature. The fainter shock feature is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME may be related to field line movement beyond the ENE limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-11-22T02:40Z. If this beyond-limb activity is the source of this CME, then there is some significant westward deflection based on triangulated measurements.
A faint minor CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and in early C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and covered by the large data gap in STEREO A COR2. No clear source has been found in EUV imagery.
